correctness.rationale: For all real m≥2,t∈[1/2,1], direct transport pairing gives ||μ_y||=(||y||_1+α|Σy_i|)/2, α=2t−1. The molecule convex hull exactly determines the unit ball. Averaging a rescaled quadratic sandwich over S_m gives an optimal Q_c(y)=||y||²_2+c(Σy_i)² for c>−1/m even against arbitrary nonsymmetric Euclidean comparison. Dual sign functionals, Sherman–Morrison inversion and molecule vertices give exact squared distortion F(c)=R(c)D(c), not mere bounds. On c≤c0 the maximum R is nonincreasing; for c≥L the component functions f_s(c) are convex and their crossing occurs only at 2α/(s+u), while the only interior stationary points of nonconstant branches are c_s. Strict endpoint coercivity and treatment of coincident branches establish an exhaustive nonempty finite candidate set; t=1/2 and 1 endpoint expressions follow by ℓ1 symmetry and the zero-sum ℓ1 hyperplane. Independent symbolic reduction verified branch and crossing identities/second derivatives. Separate numerical tests: 273 candidate-vs-one-dimensional minimizations (worst squared error 1.24×10⁻8), 180 direct molecule vertex and 180 dual facet checks, 400 optimal-transport LP tests, 23 endpoint dimensions and both rational interior examples. Finite tests are confirmatory only; the proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Numerical minimizer comparisons have finite-precision error <1.24e−8 and cover finite instances; they do not prove all real α or unbounded m.
Statement guarantees existence but not uniqueness of an optimal ellipsoid; no complex/unequal-arm assertion.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original interior Hilbert Banach–Mazur profile. The published equilateral Lipschitz-free theorem gives precisely the α=1 endpoint and is expressly excluded as an independent novelty claim; a four-point one-edge deformation and same-star numerical index do not imply the continuum optimum for three or more equal star arms. Reviewed exact Banach–Mazur direct-sum/cone and molecule-polytope literature does not imply the correlated finite-candidate optimum. Independent computational confirmation addresses correctness but not novelty. Some unindexed convex-body equivalent might exist; this is documented as risk, not ruled out by failed searches.
residual_risks: Unindexed convex-geometric treatments of ||x||_1+α|Σx_i|, symmetric ellipsoids or Lipschitz-free stars might contain an equivalent continuum formula; no absolute priority guarantee.
The α=0 tree/ℓ1 and α=1 equilateral/root-polytope endpoints are known and are not credited as independently original.
Several published mathematical findings carry the same October 11 date; relative chronological priority between records is not established.

value.rationale: Hilbertian Banach–Mazur distance is an intrinsic quantitative invariant of the finite-dimensional transportation-cost Banach spaces of a very natural equal-arm metric star. This family connects the tree ℓ1^m geometry at t=1/2 to the equilateral type-A root-polytope geometry at t=1, and the coupling α|Σy_i| creates a genuinely new continuous geometric interpolation. The finite algebraic prescription optimizes over every Euclidean isomorphism for all m≥2 and all real radii in the whole admissible interval, including nontrivial interior values, rather than reporting a few small cases or recomputing a known endpoint. A future investigator comparing embeddings, ellipsoid geometry or finite metric transportation spaces can directly use the sharp formula and the symmetric optimizer. This is motivated independent exact-invariant work, no downstream theorem required.
residual_risks: The value claim is restricted to finite equal-arm real metrics; does not classify unequal stars, general finite metrics or complex Lipschitz-free spaces.
No uniqueness of optimizers or simple global piecewise closed form is asserted; the exact finite minimization is the proven content.

final_claim: For real m≥2 and t∈[1/2,1], writing α=2t−1, the exact squared Banach–Mazur distance from the Lipschitz-free space of the m-leaf equiradial star (center-leaf t, leaf-leaf 1) to ℓ₂^m equals min_{c∈C}R(c)D(c) with precisely the candidate set and formulas in the assigned RESULT.md; an optimal pullback is Q_c=Σ y_i²+c(Σ y_i)². The t=1/2 and 1 endpoint values are m and 2 floor((m+1)/2) ceil((m+1)/2)/(m+1), respectively. Only finite real equal-arm stars.
limitations: Review covers only the real finite equiradial metric star with m≥2,t∈[1/2,1] and pairwise leaf distance normalized to 1.
The proof gives existence of a symmetric optimal Euclidean pullback, not uniqueness; no generalization to unequal-arm/infinite/complex settings.
Novelty is best-of-knowledge with explicit unindexed literature and same-date publication risks; equilateral endpoint independently published.

Raw source tree includes public-facing operational identifier and process labels in AUDIT.json, METADATA.json and REVIEW.md; their neutral replacements with byte-for-byte scientific preservation could not be staged, hence publication not ready.
